chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): When the eye blinks, or the leg kicks, or the tail moves, and you reach it, then slaughter it.

key_terms.تَحَرَّكَ الذَّنَبُ: The tail moved — third sign of life
key_terms.رَكَضَتِ الرِّجْلُ: The leg kicked — another sign of life
key_terms.طَرَفَتِ الْعَيْنُ: The eye blinked — a sign of life in the animal
key_terms.فَذَكِّهِ: Then slaughter it — imperative to perform ritual slaughter (dhakah)
key_terms.كِتَابُ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali — a foundational Shia text attributed to Imam Ali (AS), containing legal rulings, recorded by the Prophet (SAWW) and dictated to Ali (AS)

ai.seo_question: What should you do if a hunted or slaughtered animal is still showing signs of life according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This legal ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), traced back to the Book of Ali (AS), addresses the scenario of an animal that has been mortally wounded (e.g., by hunting or a failed slaughter) but still shows signs of life. If the hunter or slaughterer reaches the animal while it is still alive — indicated by a blinking eye, kicking leg, or moving tail — they must perform the ritual slaughter (dhakah) to make the animal permissible to eat. This ruling reflects the importance of completing the proper Islamic method of slaughter to ensure the animal's meat is halal.
